content.user_title: Decode Why Content Resonates and Gets Shared
content.value_statement: Audience reactions can be difficult to explain from engagement numbers alone. This skill uses textual evidence and communication theories to explain emotional responses and sharing motives.
actual_capabilities: Identify the core claim, target audience, intended action, and supporting passages in existing content.
Select one primary theory covering identity, framing, emotional appraisal, content utility, or sharing motives.
Add an auxiliary theory only when explicit textual evidence supports a distinct mechanism.
Separate textual facts, psychological inferences, and audience responses that require validation.
Distinguish motives for watching, saving, commenting, and sharing.
Produce a structured analysis with confidence levels, interpretation limits, related topics, and a focused discussion question.
limitations: Does not predict click rates, completion rates, recommendation volume, or viral outcomes.
Cannot establish actual audience emotions or behavior from text alone; comments, interviews, or behavioral data are needed.
Does not provide full line-by-line rewriting or overall commercial value assessments.
Provides an analysis workflow rather than scripts, automated analytics integrations, or independent audience measurement.

use_cases.title: Understand Responses to an Existing Post
use_cases.description: Identify which passages may activate audience identity or emotions, and distinguish possible sharing motives from unverified assumptions.

use_cases.title: Plan Evidence-Based Follow-Up Discussions
use_cases.description: Analyze an article and propose related discussion questions that preserve its main psychological mechanism without rewriting the entire piece.

use_cases.title: Develop Audience Research Hypotheses
use_cases.description: Connect textual evidence to a primary communication theory and list audience responses that interviews or behavioral data must verify.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this existing post: [text]. Explain its main audience resonance mechanism using specific passages, and identify what remains uncertain.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of one existing post.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Audience Motives
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [content] for [audience]. Distinguish watching, saving, commenting, and sharing motives. Use one primary theory and quote supporting passages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of different engagement behaviors.

prompt_templates.title: Develop Follow-Up Topics
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [article] using one primary theory. Add an auxiliary theory only if necessary. Suggest three follow-up topics that preserve the dominant mechanism.
prompt_templates.scenario: Editorial planning grounded in an existing article.

prompt_templates.title: Build Testable Mechanism Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [content] with [audience context] and [observed reactions]. Separate facts, inferences, and validation needs. Explain confidence, theoretical limits, and alternative interpretations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audience research with contextual evidence.

output_examples.input: Explain this post for junior employees: 'Asking for a clear deadline is responsible, not disrespectful.'
output: Core claim: requesting deadline clarity is legitimate professional behavior.
Primary theory: framing. The contrast between responsible and disrespectful redefines the meaning of asking.
Emotional hypothesis: readers who fear appearing difficult may feel relief. Their actual reactions require validation.
Possible sharing motive: communicate a workplace norm to colleagues. Text alone cannot establish whether readers will share.
Discussion question: how can teams make deadline clarification routine?

output_examples.input: Analyze why students might save this post: 'Before submitting your essay, check the thesis, citations, and conclusion.'
output: Primary theory: uses and gratifications. The checklist provides practical help during essay submission.
Textual evidence: the three named checks create a reusable review aid.
Likely use hypothesis: students may save the post for later reference. Confidence is moderate without behavioral data.
Interpretation limit: practical usefulness does not establish strong emotion, public agreement, or sharing behavior.
Follow-up topic: which citation mistakes should a submission checklist include?

best_practices: Provide the original content, intended audience, platform context, and any observed reactions.
Require specific textual evidence and keep one primary theory unless another explains a distinct mechanism.
Validate emotional and behavioral hypotheses with comments, interviews, or engagement data before treating them as facts.
anti_patterns: Treating theory-based analysis as a guarantee of reach, revenue, or viral performance.
Stacking theories without textual triggers or a distinct explanatory purpose.
Equating emotional activation with agreement, or agreement with actual sharing.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I provide for analysis?
faq.answer: Provide existing content and its intended audience. Platform context, comments, interviews, and behavioral data can help validate the resulting hypotheses.

faq.question: Can it predict whether my content will go viral?
faq.answer: No. It explains possible resonance and sharing mechanisms, not platform metrics or guaranteed outcomes.

faq.question: Which theories does it use?
faq.answer: Primary options cover social identity, emotional appraisal, framing, uses and gratifications, and emotional activation in sharing. Additional theories require specific triggers.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my entire article?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is mechanism analysis and discussion directions, not full line-by-line editing or overall commercial evaluation.

faq.question: Does the skill require external commands or network access?
faq.answer: The supplied files contain instructions and interface metadata. They do not include executable scripts or require network requests.
